items.stem: You have a researcher agent and a writer agent. The writer sometimes invents facts the researcher never found. What coordination fix helps most?

options.text: A hand-off contract that passes the researcher's sourced findings and instructs the writer to use only those
options.rationale: Correct: an explicit hand-off contract constrains the writer to grounded inputs.

options.text: Run both agents at a higher temperature
options.rationale: More randomness increases invention, not less.

options.text: Remove the researcher and let the writer search too
options.rationale: That removes specialisation and does not stop fabrication.
Extra tools do not constrain the writer to the researcher's findings.

items.explanation: Correct: an explicit hand-off contract constrains the writer to grounded inputs.

items.stem: Which TWO are real risks that multi-agent orchestration adds over a single agent? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Higher total token cost from inter-agent messages
options.rationale: Correct: every hand-off and message consumes tokens.

options.text: Hand-off loops where agents pass work back and forth without converging
The inability to use any tools at all
options.rationale: Multi-agent systems can still use tools; this is not a risk they add.
Coordination usually adds latency; it is not a benefit and not a risk.

items.explanation: Correct: every hand-off and message consumes tokens.

items.stem: In a supervisor topology, what is the supervisor agent primarily responsible for?

options.text: Deciding which specialist agent handles each sub-task and integrating their results
options.rationale: Correct: the supervisor routes and integrates rather than doing the specialist work itself.
That defeats delegation; specialists do the work.
Routing is unrelated to vector storage.
